feature: Isolate oversized session saves, recover refused sends, and delete image sessions without uploading history

confirmed: OkHttp 4.12.0 limits its outgoing WebSocket queue to 16 MiB, while the previous client only checked a 48 MiB wire limit.
When WebSocket.send returned false, the previous client reported NOT_SENT but retained Connected state. A subsequent small prompt could fail on the same unusable socket.
The previous deletion fix required saving full history before removeSession; the daemon also rejected saved busy projections before consulting native execution state.
diagnosis.phone_limitation: The original triggering payload size on the user's phone is not available. Oversize and refused-send behavior were reproduced locally; no claim is made that a particular phone request exceeded the limit.

changes: Limit each outbound request to 15 MiB of serialized UTF-8; bound queued bytes and reserve room for small controls before calling send.
Retire a socket immediately after send refusal or exception, publish Disconnected, and let the existing supervisor reconnect without replaying mutations.
Save one session per checkpoint request; pause an unchanged oversized snapshot and back off transient failures per session.
Adopt confirmed server blob references only for the acknowledged session version, preserving newer local events and pending operations.
Delete without a mandatory full-history save; retain local history and drafts until an explicit ACK.
For identified DeerFlow sessions, let the native deletion fence check actual execution state. Preserve protection for queued work and busy sessions without native authority.
Show actual failure reasons and prevent long status text from squeezing the message count into a vertical column.

coverage: Native confirmation removes a stale working projection.
Native busy refusal retains history and releases the deletion fence.
Queued Waku work and busy sessions without native authority remain protected.
Unknown outcomes, interrupted local cleanup, restart recovery and stale snapshot resurrection guards remain intact.

transport_tests: A real OkHttp WebSocket rejects an 18 MiB UTF-8 save locally while a subsequent prompt and removeSession succeed on the same connection.
A refused send cancels the socket and marks earlier accepted requests unknown; reconnect does not replay them.
A send exception retires the socket and preserves delivery uncertainty.
Bulk queue admission leaves room for small controls without closing the connection.
Per-session save isolation, retry backoff and version-safe canonical acknowledgement merging are covered.

device_validation.large_session: Generated-image conversation with 16 MiB synthetic padding to simulate large history
passed: Oversized save produces a per-session error without submitting it to the socket or repeatedly retrying the same snapshot.
New chat sends hi, receives the fixture response, and can be deleted on the same connection used before oversize rejection.
Busy refusal for the image conversation preserves its history and keep-this-draft input.
Force-stop and restart restore the generated image and draft.
The final build displays long save errors without collapsing the message counter.
Explicit ACK deletes the image conversation even though its full-history save is oversized.
After force-stop and restart, neither the deleted text conversation nor the image conversation returns.
Request logs show no saveTaskState upload for the large image conversation; removeSession carries the target session ID and NIL runtime.
Image preview opens and saving produces a byte-identical 10215-byte PNG in Download/deerflow.

deployment.notes: The phone's actual daemon endpoint was not identified or replaced. The active production daemon was not restarted, and no production sessions were deleted.
